title: Reel: what your fork does when you land
caption:
This is what's happening inside your fork every time you land. Oil gets pushed through a piston, and your compression clicker decides how hard that is.

Too little and it blows through and bottoms. Too much and it skips off everything. Rebound is the same oil coming back the other way.

Tell Dialed Offroad what the bike did and it tells you which clicker to move and which way, one change at a time. Link in bio.

Does your fork bottom on big landings or feel harsh on them?

title: Reel: what one click actually does
caption:
One click moves a needle a tiny bit deeper into a bleed hole. Less oil gets by, so you get more damping. That's it, and it's why one click is easy to feel, mostly in the slow stuff like braking and body weight.

And 12 out on one bike isn't 12 out on another. Every clicker has its own range, counted out from fully closed.

Dialed Offroad gives you a starting point for your bike and tells you which clicker to turn next. Link in bio.

title: Reel: POV, you copied a pro's clickers
caption:
A pro's settings are built around their weight, their springs and their speed. Copy them onto your bike and 35 fewer pounds are pushing on the same stiff springs, so the bike rides high, never settles and beats you up.

Their settings work great on their bike. Start from your own numbers instead and refine them on the bike, one change at a time.

Dialed Offroad builds a baseline from your bike, weight and track. Link in bio.
